name: M01 the replay window becomes one-sided
guards: a capture held and replayed with a FUTURE timestamp is refused too
why: Bounding only (now - t) leaves the other direction open: capture a signed request, present it with a timestamp far ahead, and 'too old' never fires. The window is |now - t| and this mutation makes it one-sided.

name: M02 an unparseable timestamp is reported as INVALID rather than STALE
guards: the three inbound refusals stay three, because they are three operator actions
why: STALE says look at a clock and INVALID says look at a secret. Collapsing the unparseable case into INVALID sends an operator to rotate a secret that was never wrong.

name: M03 the structural staleness check is deleted and the vendor's is relied on
guards: STALE is decided HERE, so it cannot collapse into the SDK's single error class
why: The SDK signals absent, stale and invalid by throwing ONE class and separates them only by an English message. Deleting our own check makes a replayed request arrive as INVALID, which is the taxonomy hostage this adapter exists to avoid.

name: M04 a present-but-empty signature header counts as signed
why: An empty header is not a signature. Accepting one would hand the request to the SDK with nothing to verify against, and what comes back is a vendor error rather than this adapter's own ABSENT.
from: return typeof value === "string" && value.trim() !== "" ? value : null;

name: M05 the bot's own message is admitted like any other
guards: an app must not run a turn on the message it just posted
why: Slack delivers the app's own post back to the app. Treating it as inbound starts a turn, whose reply is posted, which is delivered, which starts a turn: an unbounded loop costing a model call each time round and visible to the customer as the assistant talking to itself.
from: if ("botId" in event && event.botId !== undefined) return ok(ignorable(verifiedBody));

name: M06 a missing event id is synthesized from the message timestamp
guards: the admission key is the PROVIDER's own id and is never invented
why: The inbox is idempotent on [appId, eventId]. A synthesized key makes a redelivery unrecognisable, so one provider event can run two turns — and hashing the body instead would make a user who genuinely says the same thing twice get one answer.
from:

name: M07 the thread key puts the channel in the wrong segment
guards: the DOMAIN's own reader recovers the channel this adapter wrote
why: `domain/inbound.ts::extractPlatformChannelId` takes the SECOND colon-separated segment and every `channel` routing rule matches on it. A key in any other shape makes those rules silently stop matching — no error anywhere, the rule simply never fires.

name: M08 a mid-flight timeout is classified UNAVAILABLE
guards: 'did not land' and 'do not know' are different facts with different remedies
why: UNAVAILABLE means retry me, nothing happened. A request that was WRITTEN and whose response was lost may well have posted the message, so retrying posts it twice into a customer's channel. This is the single most expensive misclassification the adapter can make.

name: M09 an unrecognised throw defaults to UNAVAILABLE
guards: the classifier fails CLOSED on anything it does not understand
why: The commonest real instance is a proxy's non-JSON 502, where the request definitely left and the answer says nothing about whether the message was posted. Defaulting the unknown to RETRY is how the duplicate-message mistake gets made by a code path nobody reviewed.

name: M10 the disposition table defaults OPEN
guards: a code the table has not been taught is RECONCILE, never RETRY
why: Defaulting to retry makes every future code silently repeatable, in the one direction that duplicates a customer-visible message. A repository failure surfacing through a delivery path would become a resend.

name: M11 the API base URL loses its trailing slash
guards: the vendor resolves a method as a RELATIVE REFERENCE against this constant
why: THE REAL DEFECT THIS TRANCHE SHIPPED AND CAUGHT. `new URL('chat.postMessage', 'https://slack.com/api')` is `https://slack.com/chat.postMessage` — the `/api` segment is dropped and every outbound call 404s against a path that has never existed. Asserting the constant would not see it; asserting the vendor's own resolution does.

name: M12 the deadline timer is never cleared
guards: no per-call timer outlives its call
why: A timer left armed keeps the event loop alive, and a process that will not exit on SIGTERM because of one is a genuinely miserable thing to diagnose. The `finally` is what prevents it and nothing else does.

name: M13 a streaming edit becomes a second post
guards: streaming a turn back into a channel is an EDIT loop, not a message flood
why: `replacesProviderMessageId` is what makes a redelivered outbound event harmless — editing one message to the same text twice is indistinguishable from doing it once. Posting instead turns an at-least-once bus into a visible flood.

name: M14 an ignorable delivery is admitted to the inbox
guards: a verified event with no behaviour is acknowledged, never queued
why: Admitting reactions, joins and edits fills the inbox with rows no turn will ever run, makes the retry cap meaningless, and spends a lease on each.

name: M15 a redelivery is reported as a first delivery
guards: the transport can tell a redelivery from a first delivery
why: `duplicate` is what lets a transport answer 2xx to a redelivery while knowing no new turn was queued. Reporting every admission as new makes a redelivered event look like a second message.

name: M16 one character of the PUBLISHED vector is mistyped
guards: the external anchor is the vendor's own published vector and not a local invention
why: If a character of the transcribed body were wrong, every signature case would still pass — they would simply be testing a different, self-consistent vector this repository made up. Only the independent `node:crypto` re-derivation against the published digest notices.

name: M17 the upgrade differential compares the shipped line with itself
guards: the two lines under comparison are two independently published artifacts
why: If the audited alias ever resolved to the same install as the primary dependency, every case in the differential would compare a function with itself and pass forever — a green suite proving nothing about the 4.34 -> 4.40 move.

name: M18 the far side records a request only when it answers one
guards: what the far side RECEIVED is independent of whether it replied
why: The whole instrument. If `received` were appended only on the answering path, the timeout cases could no longer ask 'the adapter reported a failure — did the message actually land?', and every one of them would go quietly green against a server that had the message in hand.

name: M19 the directory stays on UNIMPLEMENTED_ADAPTERS after gaining a constructor
guards: rule (C7) joins the unimplemented list to the adapter packages' own source
why: A readiness endpoint that says 'this directory is a generated interface' about a directory that has a working constructor is lying to an operator about why their channel is not serving. C7 reads the list back and joins it to the filesystem in BOTH directions.
